title: Feature request: multi-cursor support for `<textarea>` and `contenteditable`

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Currently, `<textarea>` and `contenteditable>` support only a single caret and selection. This limits advanced editing workflows, including:

- Multi-line or column editing (like batch editing multiple entries)  
- Simultaneous edits at multiple positions (common in code, structured text, or tables)  
- Syntax-aware editing, such as highlighting, coloring, or inline annotations  

Today, developers must rely on fully custom editors (CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace) to achieve these features. If web standards ever want to switch from content editable divs to [richer text fields](https://open-ui.org/components/richer-text-fields.explainer/), we need foundational features like **multiple cursors** also if we should be able to make the switch. with feature like `Highlight` for textarea we might one day see the potential of having syntax coloring with just a simple `<textarea>` instead of having lots of dom elements.  


### What solutions exist today?

- **Custom editor frameworks** (CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace) simulate multi-cursors, syntax highlighting, and rich annotations.  
- **Contenteditable hacks** are used for rich text, but they often suffer from performance, IME, and accessibility issues.  
- There is **no native API** for multi-cursor or multi-range selection in `<textarea>` or contenteditable, which prevents standard web fields from achieving parity with desktop editors.  


### How would you solve it?

Introduce a **multi-cursor / multi-selection API** for `<textarea>` and `contenteditable>`:

- Allows multiple carets and selection ranges simultaneously  
- Enables richer editing workflows (batch edits, multi-line formatting, inline highlighting)  
- Complements future “richer textarea” features like syntax coloring, inline annotations, and semantic highlighting  
- Leaves implementation details open — browsers could expose ranges, render carets, or allow JS libraries to hook into a standard API  


### Anything else?

- Multi-cursor is not just for developers; it’s **part of making web-native text fields richer and more powerful**, closing the gap between `<textarea>` and modern editors.  
- It supports accessibility and IME correctness better than fully JavaScript-based hacks.  
- It aligns with the vision described in the [Open UI Richer Text Fields explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/richer-text-fields.explainer/) — a native, semantic, extensible, and accessible editable experience.
